# **Assignment 6**

In this assignment, you will use R (within R-Studio) to:

+ Load an untidy data set
+ Tidy it using tidyr and dplyr verbs
+ Plot it with ggplot


**All file paths should be relative, starting from *your* Assignment_6 directory!!**

**This means that you need to create a new R-Project named "Assignment_6.Rproj" in your Assignment_6 directory, and work from scripts within that.**

First, we can load the *tidyverse* package and import an untidy data set

```{r, echo=TRUE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
dat <- read_csv("../../Data/BioLog_Plate_Data.csv") # you may need to modify this path to fit where this file is stored relative to your assignment 6 script
```

As you might be able to tell from the column names, this data set is all about the ability of various environmental samples to utilize different carbon sources. Each plate has 96 wells and in each well is a fluorescently labeled carbon source. You dilute an environmental sample and add it to each of the wells in a plate and then read light absorbance over time. Higher absorbance values indicate more utilization of that carbon source by the microbes present in the sample. 

```{r, echo=FALSE,out.width=300}
knitr::include_graphics("../../../media/Ecoplate1.jpg")
```

Here, we have real data from 4 environmental samples (two soil and two water samples), and their absorbance values at 24, 48, and 144 hours. These plate experiments were repeated at 3 increasing dilutions for each sample source.

# Your task is to Write an R script that:

library(gganimate)

#1.  Cleans this data into tidy (long) form #

# The tidy_biolog offers a new name for a newly created object that after running will now be in tidy form ##
## pivot_longer allows me to change the columns and rows and in this instance the cols beginning with Hr_ are being changed to be labeled as time and the values were changed to have the label absorbance ##
## The mutate script tells R studio to change the values in the column time to be just the number which drops the Hr_ making graphing in the future much easier ##

tidy_biolog <- dat |>
  pivot_longer(
  cols = starts_with("Hr_"),
  names_to = "Time",
  values_to = "Absorbance"
) |> 
mutate(
  Time = parse_number(Time))

## This simple tidy_biolog pops up what the new object has as rows and columns and allows me to check if my script worked correctly ##

tidy_biolog


2.  Creates a new column specifying whether a sample is from soil or water

# tidy_biolog tells R Studio to use the data in tidy_biolog and mutate tells R Studio to add a new column ##
## Type = names the new column Type ##
## if_else takes anything labeled as soil as a soil sample and if it does not contain soil it calls the sample a water sample ##

tidy_biolog <- tidy_biolog |>
  mutate(
    Type = if_else(str_detect(`Sample ID`, "Soil"), "Soil", "Water")
)

## This simple tidy_biolog allows me to check if the script worked ##  

tidy_biolog


3.  Generates a plot that matches this one (note just plotting dilution == 0.1):

## This plot_data creates a new object and first filters out just the dilution == 0.1 ##
## summarize generates a mean value for the mean absorbance which is what generates only two lines on the graphs and without it it produces a whole bunch of zig zag lines ## 

plot_data <- tidy_biolog |> 
  filter(Dilution == 0.1) |> 
  group_by(Type, Substrate, Time) |> 
  summarize(mean_absorbance = mean(Absorbance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")



## ggplot tells R studio to plot using gg plot with x as time and y uses the data points from mean_absorbance which was created in the last script ##
## geom_line generates a lateral line with a width of 0.8 and facet wrap and scale y generate how the graphs are generated and adding limits from 0,2 allowed me to make the graphs look just like the one in the assignment ##
## Labs generates labels for the X axis, the y axis, a title, and color = Type tells ggplot to add different colors for each of the different types in that column ## 
## theme allows me to generate a legend and the element_text allows me to dictate the size of the strip text, the axis text, and where the legend appears on the image ## 


ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Time, y = mean_absorbance, color = Type)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ Substrate, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 2)) +  
  labs(
    title = "Just dilution 0.1",
    x = "Time",
    y = "Absorbance",
    color = "Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.position = "right"
  )





```{r, echo=FALSE,out.width=600}
knitr::include_graphics("../../../media/biolog.png")
```

4.  Generates an animated plot that matches this one (absorbance values are mean of all 3 replicates for each group):

This plot is just showing values for the substrate "Itaconic Acid"

## anim_data is being generated as a new object that adds a filter for the substrate Itaconic acid #3
## They are grouped by Sample_ID Dilution and time, then summarize generates the mean absorbance ## 

anim_data <- tidy_biolog |> 
  filter(Substrate == "Itaconic Acid") |> 
  group_by(`Sample ID`, Dilution, Time) |> 
  summarize(mean_absorbance = mean(Absorbance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")


## p <- generates a new object based on all of the things after that symbol ##
## ggplot generates scatter plots based on the X = time, y is the mean_absorbance and the color is based on sample ID lables##
## labs adds labels to the graphs including an X label a Y and the color labels ## 
## The limits make the graphs look just like one in the assignment ## 
## gganimate tells gganimate to animate the lines and reveal them over the time provided in the graphs ## 



p <- ggplot(anim_data, aes(x = Time, y = mean_absorbance, color = `Sample ID`)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ Dilution) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 2.5)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time",
    y = "Mean Absorbance",
    color = "Sample ID"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 8)
  ) +
  gganimate::transition_reveal(Time)
  
  
## This final line tells the gganimate to animate the object p and how to animate it to look like the one in the assignment ##   
  
gganimate::animate(p, nframes = 100, fps = 10, width = 700, height = 500)
